findings.claim: groundUnderBody still allocates two arrays on every call: the `ts` literal and the `hs` array from `ts.map` with a closure. visualPose also returns a fresh `{ y, pitch }` object. Both run for every car on every tick through carViews→carView, so a 6-car race makes about 18 short-lived allocations per tick. C027 (closed) only removed the groundAt default object and the per-ramp `[-1e-6, -r.length]` array; these allocations were left.
findings.evidence: src/sim/car.ts:196 `const ts = [-half, 0, half];`, :203/:205 `ts.push(...)`, :207 `return { ts, hs: ts.map((t) => groundAt(track, car.x + fx * t, car.z + fz * t, ground).h) };`; :168 `return { y, pitch };`, :188 `return y >= car.y ? { y, pitch } : { y: car.y, pitch: 0 };`; caller :137 `const { y, pitch } = visualPose(car, track, speed);`. In perf.json, groundUnderBody (main:162) is 1205 B/frame on bends, 1865 on dust-bowl and 1322 on hay-loop. visualPose (main:121) is 1173 B/frame on dust-bowl.
findings.suggestedFix: Add module scratch next to `ground` (car.ts:325): `const bodyTs: number[] = []; const bodyHs: number[] = [];`. In groundUnderBody, reset with `bodyTs.length = 0`, push `-half, 0, half` and then the lips and feet in the same order. Fill bodyHs with a plain loop that calls the same groundAt, and return nothing; visualPose then reads bodyTs/bodyHs. Have visualPose write into a scratch `pose = { y: 0, pitch: 0 }` that carView reads straight away. The float operations and their order stay the same, so replays are bit-identical.

findings.claim: tick() replaces r.curr with a new array from carViews(r.world) on every sim tick: one `map` array plus one new CarView per car. Nothing keeps those views beyond the next tick. draw() copies them into r.drawn, ui.sync reads x/z only, and state() deep-copies. A two-buffer swap would remove all of these per-tick allocations.
findings.evidence: src/game.ts:183-184 `r.prev = r.curr; r.curr = carViews(r.world);`; src/sim/world.ts:121-123 `return world.cars.map((car) => carView(car, world.track));`; src/sim/car.ts:138-148 builds a new 9-field object per car. Readers: game.ts:189 interpolate (Object.assign into r.drawn), :193 ui.sync (race-ui.ts:139-146 copies x/z), :301 state() `race.curr.map((c) => ({ ...c }))`. perf.json: hay-loop carView (main:98) 780 B/frame; `map ((native))` 1127 B/frame bends, 1111 hay-loop.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `carViewsInto(world, out: CarView[])` in src/sim/world.ts, which Object.assigns carView(car, track) into out[i], or writes the fields in place to avoid even the temporary. In startRace, create prev and curr as two distinct arrays (`views` and `views.map((v) => ({ ...v }))`). In tick(), swap them (`const t = r.prev; r.prev = r.curr; r.curr = t; carViewsInto(r.world, r.curr);`). The values are the same, so drawing and the UI are unchanged. game.ts is likely touched by open PR #30 (B08), so apply it after that lands.

confirmations.note: src/game.ts:188 `const view = raceView(r.world);` still runs in draw() every animation frame, tick or not. raceView (world.ts:126-135) still allocates distances, positions() (race.ts:95-113: order, sort closure, result) and a RacerView with lapTicks.slice() per racer. play() at game.ts:322 also calls it per tick. perf.json bends: sort 996, map 1127 B/frame.
